comparison: Use AntitoneOn for f1 on the unit interval, allowing flat portions. In the nondegenerate mixture 0<pi0<1 with the positive mixture-density version, pi0/(pi0+(1-pi0)*f1) is nondecreasing exactly when f1 is nonincreasing. The source allows pi0 endpoints elsewhere: at pi0=1 the posterior is constant and imposes no restriction on the unused alternative density; at pi0=0 it is zero on positive-density observations and requires a convention at zero density. Thus the printed equivalence cannot be used unconditionally at those endpoints. Preserve the source claim and recorded limitation rather than strengthening all statements to the interior case. In Theorem 1 this assumption applies only to the final max-lfdr clause, not its preceding last-rejection identity.
gap: Order predicates express the shape condition; the posterior equivalence needs the nondegenerate mixture and density-version qualifications recorded from the source.

The predicates preserve non-strict monotonicity, while the Bayes-ratio equivalence fails to recover f1's shape at degenerate mixture proportions.

comparison: The candidate density averages a Gaussian of mean Pi*g*theta and covariance sigma^2 times the identity over the supplied rotation law Lambda. Preserve the projected output dimension in the normalization and exponent denominator, and take the unprojected case by Pi=identity with dimension d. The group-averaged density is a Gaussian mixture, not generally a single Gaussian whose mean is the group-averaged mean. R_n is the negative mean sample log-density, whereas R is its expectation under the fixed true law p_(theta-star), not the candidate law p_theta. Equality E[R_n]= -E[log p_theta(Y)] requires the common marginal law and integrability; it is not a definition of expectation under the empirical law. The intended Gaussian density requires sigma>0 and a Euclidean norm, and logarithmic positivity/integrability must be justified rather than using Real.log(0)=0 or the Bochner integral's zero fallback. The generic Gaussian law declaration does not itself provide this exact Haar-mixture density formula or its differentiability.
gap: Gaussian laws, logarithms and integrals provide the components; the exact mixture density and its positivity, integrability and population-likelihood identities require model-specific proofs.
searches: Search negative/population log-likelihood terminology and Gaussian density support; inspect multivariateGaussian, Real.log and the Bochner integral against (2.3)/(2.5)
Generic Gaussian measures and integration are available, but a group mixture cannot be replaced by a single Gaussian and the true-law expectation remains distinct from the candidate density.

comparison: Index the product law by triples (t,i,j) with t in [T] and 1<=i<j<=n, and assign each coordinate Bernoulli-rho with inclusion atom first. The product construction uses probability measures and yields joint independence across all observed edges and layers. It is not a law on two independently sampled symmetric entries or on self-loops; reverse entries of a displayed adjacency matrix are the same observation and the diagonal is not modeled here. There are no community or layer labels under this null. Both testing hypotheses are compared on the observed graph tensor, not on an enlarged sample containing latent labels. Endpoint rho values can define degenerate Bernoulli laws even if later likelihood-ratio results need interior parameters.
gap: Bernoulli product measures suffice for the null model once the observed upper-triangular edge index set is supplied.
searches: Inspect bernoulliMeasure and infinitePi against Definition 1(2) and the saved observation-domain note
The product law gives the required joint independence on the selected edge/layer coordinates without introducing labels or independent mirror entries.

comparison: Quantify over a sequence of measurable binary tests on the observed graph tensor and require the sum P1(test=0)+P0(test=1) to tend to zero along the given model sequence. The tests may vary with n; a fixed test for all dimensions is not required. The two errors use their respective laws on the same observation space, with latent assignments marginalized rather than supplied to the test. On probability measures both terms are finite and nonnegative, so their real-valued sum is legitimate and vanishing forces each error to vanish. This defines strong detection, not exact community recovery. Its negation says no such vanishing-error sequence exists and does not by itself imply total variation tends to zero or that every nontrivial weak test fails; the paper's separate chi-square theorem supplies stronger evidence in its own regime.
gap: Measurable-test quantification and ordinary convergence express strong distinguishability; stronger impossibility conclusions require separate results.
searches: Search distinguishability and strong-detection terms in Probability/InformationTheory; inspect Tendsto and the source's saved recovery/detection-strength note
The definition is an ordinary limit of total testing error; a generic limit predicate does not prove equivalence to stronger non-detection notions.

comparison: Use Set.pi over the full coordinate index set to select an arbitrary tuple of coordinate laws from their respective families, then map that tuple to the product probability measure. The model class is the image of these law tuples, not merely a Cartesian product whose elements are tuples rather than joint distributions. Similarly theta ranges over the unrestricted Cartesian product of the Theta_j and its law is the product of p_(theta_j). Coordinates may have different spaces and families; no common scalar parameter, identical distribution, exponential-family form or continuity is built into this definition. Every selected law must be a probability measure, since infinitePi returns zero otherwise. Independence concerns coordinates of one observation; an i.i.d. sample of n observations requires a separate product construction. Later existence of two parameter points at a given Hellinger scale does not establish continuity of the entire parameter map.
gap: Cartesian sets and product probability measures express the model class without a further library gap; coordinate-family restrictions remain theorem-specific.

The constructions distinguish a tuple of marginal laws from its joint product law and impose no common-parameter or continuity condition.
